QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_6

question.text: Ms. Kavita Rao, a family office CIO, briefs Mr. Suresh Patel (Manager of Kaveri Private Credit AIF - Category II): 'Our patriarch wants medium-to-long horizon exposure to later-stage unlisted companies whose business plans have already been validated by institutional investors; he has deep pockets and high illiquidity tolerance, and is agnostic to debt or equity.' Which AIF product set BEST matches this investor profile per the Chapter 3 suitability illustrations?

answer.text: Category I Angel Funds and early-stage VC funds, because the family office has high risk appetite
Category II Private Equity Funds, Private Debt Funds (including venture debt) and Special Situation Funds
Category III Hedge Funds using long-short and market-neutral strategies
Listed-market PMS with a concentrated small-cap mandate

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Illustration 2 in Section 3.4.1, an investor with medium-to-long term horizon, deep pockets, high illiquidity tolerance, seeking 'growth oriented unlisted companies that have potential to go public or get acquired' and wanting institutional validation fits 'very well with Category II private equity funds which specialise in larger deals in validated companies'. Being agnostic to debt/equity broadens the allocation to Cat II debt and special-situation funds as well (per Illustration 3). The Trap: Option A describes Illustration 1 (smaller tickets, high-risk early-stage) — wrong profile. Option C is Cat III territory and is excluded from Cat I/II suitability testing. Option D is listed-securities PMS (XXI-B scope), not AIF. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests the same Illustration-2 pattern from the distributor-recommendation side. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) covers listed-PMS suitability. Cat III suitability is XIX-E-era and is NOT tested at Cat I/II level. Manager's Pro-Tip: Family offices with 'deep pockets + patient capital' are the natural anchor LPs for Cat II PE funds; negotiate an advisory committee seat and information rights in exchange for their anchor ticket, and document the anchor economics (fee rebate, co-invest rights) in a side letter — never in the main LPA.
